provenance: [REVIEWED] Question set: research/v3/ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md group A (ground structure). Vocabularies copied verbatim from that table, plus the two additions documented in `deviations`.
design_notes: Variant A asks the four structure questions in the order the question set lists them: ground_type first, then shading_geometry, field_texture, enclosure.

Variant B (group-a.variant-b.json) asks the same four questions in a different order with independently written stems, per ALBUM_ARTWORK_SEMANTIC_ORACLE_PIPELINE.md §3: a label that survives both wordings is robust to framing.
Greedy decoding, so prompt variation is the only source of a disagreement signal (pipeline §3).
Output keys are short and every answer is a closed-vocabulary token, per pipeline §10 lever 1 (decode length dominates cost).
deviations: ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md marks shading_geometry as '(when shaded)'. A fixed JSON schema cannot make a field conditional without a union, so the vocabulary gains `not_applicable` and the prompt says when to use it. The analysis treats `not_applicable` and a missing answer identically.

`note` is the question set's `ambiguity_note`. HUMAN AUDIT ONLY — never read by code (pipeline §0). It is required by the schema and capped at 120 characters so the decode cost is bounded; the prompt asks for an empty string when confidence is high.
system: You label album cover artwork for a research dataset. You answer only with the exact words offered. You never explain, never add fields, never use words that were not offered.
prompt:
Look at this album cover.

Answer four questions about its GROUND — the large areas behind and around any subject, text or figures. Ignore small elements, ignore what the cover is "about", ignore whether it is attractive.

The distinction that matters most: a surface with light and shadow falling across it is ONE ground, even though its colour changes. A photograph of sky above grass is TWO grounds, because the sky and the grass are different things that happen to sit next to each other.

1. ground — what is the ground made of?
   flat_field — one area of essentially one colour, no shading
   shaded_field — one surface whose colour changes smoothly across it (light, shadow, glow, fade)
   multiple_distinct_fields — two or more separate areas of different colour meeting at a boundary
   full_scene — a depicted space with depth: a room, a landscape, a street, a place
   pattern_or_texture — a repeating motif or a material surface covering the whole ground
   none_discernible — no ground can be made out

2. shading — if you answered shaded_field, how is the shading arranged?
   linear — the colour changes along one direction, edge to edge
   radial_or_vignette — the colour changes outward from a centre, or darkens toward the corners
   irregular — neither; the shading has no simple geometry
   not_applicable — you did not answer shaded_field

3. texture — does the ground's colour variation read as the grain of one material, or as separate coloured areas?
   smooth — no visible grain or texture
   one_textured_material — grain, paper, film noise, brush marks, halftone: one material throughout
   distinct_areas — the variation is separate coloured areas, not the texture of a material

4. enclosure — is the artwork enclosed by a border or bars?
   none — the artwork runs to the edge
   thin_border — a narrow frame or keyline
   thick_frame_or_bars — a wide frame, or solid bars along one or more edges, large enough to be an area of its own

Then:
   confidence — high, medium, or low, for your answers taken together
   note — leave this an empty string when confidence is high; otherwise at most one short sentence saying what is ambiguous

Reply with JSON only.
